title: arXiv Physics — Monday, 9 November 2026 batch
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-recent-paper ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart. Citation evidence is limited for this very fresh batch, so the ordering reflects concrete results, cross-archive relevance, and identifiable analysis or code/data evidence rather than measured popularity.

sections.title: arXiv Physics — Monday, 9 November 2026 batch
sections.content: 11 notable recent papers selected from 390 unique works. The dominant pattern is quantum-enabled measurement and modeling connecting fundamental questions to practical platforms. Agenda: monitored quantum transport, milligram-scale gravity, QCD and nuclear constraints, then detector and cosmology methods.

sections.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era – observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
sections.abstract: The authors report superconducting-processor measurements of first-arrival distributions in periodically monitored spin chains and circuits, resolving a crossover between quantum-Zeno suppression and a low-monitoring regime for single and interacting particles in one and two dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the optimal monitoring period tracks the single-particle bandwidth and that the crossover persists with interactions and in 2D; they describe this as the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in monitored quantum transport.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; superconducting quantum hardware with mid-circuit measurements, compared with quantum-trajectory theory
sections.unique_caveat: This uses the repeated-projective-measurement definition on lattice models; arrival-time distributions depend on the detection protocol and there is no universally accepted arrival-time observable.

sections.title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
sections.abstract: The authors use microwave optomechanical readout at millikelvin temperatures to measure the force from a coherently displaced 87 mg source mass on a 1.3 mg test mass, reporting a two-order-of-magnitude advance in small-mass gravity sensing and improved sensitivity at kHz frequencies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe a force with the expected distance dependence and infer a gravitational constant consistent with CODATA within their stated 1σ systematic uncertainties; the experiment is a sensing advance, not a demonstration of quantum gravity.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; cryogenic microwave optomechanical membrane, moving gold source mass, and calibrated homodyne readout
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred gravitational constant has sizeable statistical and systematic uncertainty; the masses are not prepared in non-classical motional states, which the authors identify as a future goal.

sections.title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
sections.abstract: The authors derive an estimator for the light-quark-mass response of QCD topological susceptibility from correlations on a single fixed-mass ensemble and find that this response rises from about one toward two across the chiral crossover.
sections.claimed_result: In (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD, the local logarithmic mass slope of topological susceptibility changes from roughly linear to roughly quadratic dependence across the crossover, with an effective amplitude peaking near the crossover.
sections.evidence_type: computational; lattice-QCD ensembles at a pion mass near 220 MeV over temperatures below and above the crossover
sections.unique_caveat: The light quarks are heavier than physical, and the continuum/discretization check is made at a representative temperature rather than across the full temperature scan.

sections.title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
sections.abstract: Using nuclear shell-model transition densities, the authors test a proposed explanation for the roughly 20% deficit in measured electron-neutrino captures on gallium and conclude that realistic densities do not remove the discrepancy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find factorized and nonfactorized cross sections remain about 20% above the measured value, and that matching it with their single-nucleon-density ansatz requires fine-tuned, unusually large transition densities.
sections.evidence_type: computational; nuclear shell-model transition densities normalized to the 71Ge electron-capture half-life and folded with calculated electron wavefunctions
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion tests the proposed mechanism within the shell-model interactions, operators, and valence spaces studied; it does not resolve the gallium anomaly itself.

sections.title: Just CaloCHILL: fast hadronic shower generation in a learned latent space
sections.abstract: CaloCHILL generates calorimeter showers by modeling a compressed latent representation and then decompressing it into timed detector hits; on simulated positive-pion showers it reproduces key observables and is reported to be 600 times faster than its predecessor.
sections.claimed_result: On Geant4 positive-pion showers in the proposed International Large Detector calorimeter, the three-stage latent-space model reproduces main spatial, energy, and timing observables and improves the reported accuracy metrics while running 600× faster than its predecessor.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Geant4-generated showers for a proposed FCC-ee detector, evaluated against simulated shower distributions
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark is limited to simulated positive-pion showers and a proposed detector configuration; it is not validation on beam-test data or proof of transfer to other particle types.

sections.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption for both TE and TM polarizations in a germanium metasurface on doped indium arsenide, measuring a 0.035 absorptivity difference under field reversal at 16.6 μm and 0.48 T.
sections.claimed_result: The authors attribute the TE response to the metasurface coupling light into field components that let the InAs magneto-optic response act on both polarizations, enabling dual-polarization nonreciprocity with a permanent-magnet field.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on doped InAs under a 0.48 T Halbach-array field
sections.unique_caveat: The reported contrast is for a specific structure, wavelength, angle, and field; proposed heat-transfer and energy applications are not demonstrated by this measurement alone.

sections.title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
sections.abstract: The authors develop two flux-conservative numerical formulations for causal, stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in general spacetimes, prove well-posedness properties, and simulate examples ranging from heavy-ion collisions to accretion flows.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove two formulations equivalent to or consistent with the BDNK system and show that BDNK and minimal Israel–Stewart descriptions can differ substantially at larger shear viscosity in their boost-invariant heavy-ion simulations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; flux-conservative solvers, fixed black-hole backgrounds, and heavy-ion simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and TRENTo initial conditions
sections.unique_caveat: The applications use selected flow setups and fixed spacetime backgrounds; the reported difference from Israel–Stewart is conditional on the modeled viscosity and initialization, not a direct experimental discrimination.

sections.title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
sections.abstract: The authors calculate how medium-induced momentum broadening, radiative corrections, and jet-sourced medium response affect the back-to-back angular structure of transverse energy-energy correlators in heavy-ion dijet events.
sections.claimed_result: For the model parameters studied, the authors find broadening lowers the back-to-back TEEC peak, radiative corrections suppress it further and enhance larger-angle decorrelations, while the mean medium response contributes broadly across azimuth.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; NLL′ resummation combined with first-order-in-coupling medium modifications for a color-singlet quark–antiquark pair in a homogeneous medium
sections.unique_caveat: The calculation uses an idealized homogeneous medium and color-singlet hard process; these predicted patterns are not themselves an observation in heavy-ion data.

sections.title: Successive Decimetric Bursts Associated with Breakout Magnetic Reconnection during the Decay Phase of an M-Class Flare
sections.abstract: Using MUSER radio imaging spectroscopy and SDO data for a 2014 M1.1 solar flare, the authors associate successive decimetric bursts during the flare's decay phase with electron acceleration near a quasi-separatrix layer during breakout reconnection.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the radio source coincides with a high-squashing-factor region and interpret the successive bursts as consistent with nonthermal electrons accelerated by breakout reconnection.
sections.evidence_type: observational; MUSER (0.4–2 GHz) radio imaging spectroscopy, SDO observations, and nonlinear force-free field extrapolations of a single flare
sections.unique_caveat: This is one event; the reconnection and pseudostreamer acceleration account is an interpretation supported by the radio and field-model analysis, not a general result established across solar flares.

sections.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
sections.abstract: The authors test whether selected primordial sharp/resonant features can be confused with two post-inflationary mechanisms in CMB anisotropies, finding no significant degeneracy for the representative models and likelihoods they analyze.
sections.claimed_result: In the considered examples, exotic energy injection and early dark energy do not generically reproduce the characteristic running oscillations of primordial features, and adding the studied feature classes does not significantly change the posteriors.
sections.evidence_type: computational; principal-component and full-likelihood analyses of representative primordial and post-inflationary CMB signal models
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call this an initial investigation: primordial feature families and post-inflationary mechanisms are restricted, with the latter implemented phenomenologically.

sections.title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
sections.abstract: The authors present a two-stage search and machine-learning classification pipeline for transients in simulated LISA data, reporting close to 98% classification accuracy and processing a month of data in under two minutes on a laptop.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report near-98% classification accuracy on their simulated test and month-scale data processing in under two minutes on a laptop, proposing use as a low-latency summary/alert stage.
sections.evidence_type: computational; transient search and machine-learning classification tested on simulated LISA data
sections.unique_caveat: These are initial results on simulated data; the paper discusses framework limitations, and performance on realistic LISA noise and global-fit analyses remains to be demonstrated.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
content: Quantum experiments meet measurement theory: monitored arrival-time measurements (2611.09814) and milligram-scale optomechanical gravity sensing (2611.08619) are distinct platform demonstrations, not observations of quantum gravity.

Nuclear and relativistic matter across scales: lattice QCD (2611.09150), gallium transition densities (2611.09788), BDNK hydrodynamics (2611.09582), and TEEC calculations (2611.08579) link nuclear structure, hot QCD, relativistic fluids, and heavy-ion observables; these are not independent confirmations.

Simulation and inference for detector design: CaloCHILL (2611.08606) models timed calorimeter showers; a LISA pipeline (2611.08880) classifies simulated signals and glitches. Real-data performance remains to be demonstrated.

Model and event generality: the CMB feature comparison (2611.08585) tests restricted signal families, while the solar study (2611.09332) analyzes one flare; broader models and observations are needed.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
content: Arrival-time protocol dependence is noted by the authors of 2611.09814; compare alternative detector couplings and test scaling with chain length, particle number, and device noise.
Thermal force noise and non-gravitational couplings limit 2611.08619; reduce thermal noise, vary source geometry and drive frequency, and repeat calibration before pursuing non-classical mass states.
The QCD scan in 2611.09150 uses heavier-than-physical light quarks and a discretization check at one temperature; extend multiple lattice spacings across the crossover and approach physical masses.

The shell-model test in 2611.09788 leaves the gallium deficit unresolved; independent nuclear calculations and better transition-strength constraints could test nuclear versus experimental contributions.
CaloCHILL (2611.08606) and the LISA pipeline (2611.08880) need independent validation beyond their simulated benchmarks, across detector-like data and varied particle/noise conditions.
The single-event solar interpretation (2611.09332) and restricted CMB model families (2611.08585) motivate multi-event radio analyses and broader, more realistic cosmological likelihood models.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The batch's strongest papers pair sharply posed physical questions with controllable experiments or reusable computational methods. Several conclusions remain specific to their models, hardware, or simulated datasets and need independent validation or broader measurements.
